hypothesis: After a confirmed swing, the first rejection of a Fibonacci retracement level may outperform the 0.5 midpoint and a buy-and-hold control across stocks and timeframes.
parameter_rationale: Confirmed pivot wings 3 and 5 bars; retracements 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.786; rejection zone 0.25 or 0.5 ATR. All 16 combinations fixed before results. 0.5 is a non-Fibonacci midpoint control at equal wing/tolerance.
baseline: 25% long buy-and-hold on the same candles, next-open execution and identical transaction costs; 0.5 retracement is a location control.
signal_rule: At close i, use only pivots confirmed at least wing+1 bars earlier: low pivot before high pivot defines bullish impulse, high before low defines bearish. Impulse amplitude >=2 times current ATR14. Long: first bar whose low is within tolerance*ATR14 of high - ratio*(high-low) and closes above level. Short: mirrored high touch of low + ratio*(high-low) and close below. Once per anchor pair. Exit long on close below confirmed low, short on close above confirmed high; opposite entry also reverses. Orders next bar open. No current/future pivot is used.
cost_status: after_30bps_round_trip_transaction_cost_equivalent; excludes dividends, short borrow and exchange lots
selection: Compare yearly PnL, monthly profitable share and downside against buy-and-hold and the 0.5 midpoint on matched symbols/timeframes; research only, no automatic paper promotion without parity and corporate-action review.
limitations: TradingView levels are manually anchored; this is a mechanical confirmed-pivot interpretation.
Pivot confirmation lags by wing+1 bars and is not painted on the original pivot at decision time.
Only selected ratio and tolerance grid tested; no claim of unique golden-ratio advantage.
Dividends, splits, short borrow and lots not fully modelled.
